climate.overview_html: The headline update on September 14 is the Copernicus Climate Change Service September 10 bulletin confirming that August 2026 was the world’s joint-hottest month on record, tied with July 2023 at 1.65°C above the pre-industrial baseline — the second consecutive month to cross the 1.5°C Paris threshold — with extra-polar SSTs setting an all-time August record at 21.07°C and 13.2% of global surfaces registering record-high August temperatures. The Atlantic hurricane drought continues to extend: as of September 14 the basin is now 105+ consecutive days without a hurricane, surpassing the record set September 12, and the NHC Tropical Weather Outlook is showing a 20% formation probability for a subtropical low forming in the central Atlantic — too early and too far north to be a traditional MDR system, but it marks the first any-probability Atlantic area in weeks. NOAA’s Super El Niño forecast holds at 97% probability with ONI tracking ~+3.6°C for SON, supporting 2027 as the primary candidate for a new all-time global temperature record. The Nepal–Tibet toll remains at 1,412+ dead and ~5,651+ missing with no significant change since September 11.

items.headline: Copernicus August 2026 Bulletin: Joint-Hottest Month on Record (Tied July 2023) at 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial; Extra-Polar SSTs All-Time August Record 21.07°C; 13.2% of Global Surfaces Set Record-High August Temperatures; 16th Consecutive Month ≥1.5°C
items.summary: Copernicus Climate Change Service's September 10 monthly bulletin confirms August 2026 as the world's joint-hottest month on record, tied with July 2023 at 1.65°C above the pre-industrial baseline (1850–1900 average). August 2026 was the 16th consecutive month at or above the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold. Extra-polar sea surface temperatures set an all-time August record at 21.07°C. 13.2% of global land and ocean surfaces registered record-high temperatures for any August day during the month. The joint-record status (tied with July 2023, the previous absolute monthly record) means the three hottest months in recorded history now include two months from a single El Niño year: July 2023 and August 2026. The August 2026 global mean surface air temperature exceeded the 1991–2020 ERA5 climatology by approximately 0.71°C.

items.headline: Atlantic Hurricane Season: Record Now 105+ Days Without a Hurricane; NHC Tropical Weather Outlook Shows First Atlantic Formation Area in Weeks — 20% Subtropical Low, Central Atlantic, Non-MDR Track; Eastern Pacific Counter-Pattern Continues
items.summary: As of September 14, 2026, the Atlantic hurricane season has extended its satellite-era record for the longest stretch without a hurricane to 105+ consecutive days since June 1 — adding two more days beyond the record set on September 12. In a notable development, the NHC's Tropical Weather Outlook now shows a 20% formation probability for a subtropical area of low pressure in the central Atlantic. The system is located far north of the climatological Main Development Region — well above 30°N — and is not forecast to follow a standard tropical development pathway; it would be a subtropical rather than a tropical cyclone if it develops. Five named tropical storms have formed (Arthur through Edouard), none reaching hurricane strength. The Super El Niño's anomalous upper-level westerly shear continues to suppress the MDR, while the Eastern Pacific remains in its inverse counter-surge mode with 15+ named storms.

items.source: Fox Weather / NOAA CPC / EarthSky / Washington Post
items.headline: NOAA El Niño Update: 97% Probability of Super El Niño This Fall–Winter; 75% Probability of Record-Breaking Event Exceeding 1997–98 and 2015–16; Niño 3.4 Anomaly Tracking ~3.6°C for SON; 2027 Primary Candidate for All-Time Temperature Record
items.summary: NOAA's September forecast cycle maintains a 97% probability that the current El Niño event will reach Super El Niño status (3-month ONI ≥+2.0°C) during fall-winter 2026/27 and 75% probability of exceeding both the 1997–98 and 2015–16 records (ONI ≥+2.5°C). Climate scientist Daniel Swain places approximately 70% probability on 2026 becoming the strongest El Niño since at least 1950, with peak intensity projected between October and December 2026. WMO's multi-model SON 2026 ensemble places the Niño 3.4 SST anomaly at approximately +3.6°C for September–November. With global temperature anomalies typically lagging El Niño SST peaks by 3–6 months, 2027 is the primary candidate for a new all-time global surface temperature record, building on the base already established by August 2026's record 1.65°C above pre-industrial.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse GLOF: Toll Holds at 1,412+ Dead (1,369 Nepal + 43 Tibet); ~5,651+ Missing; Barrier Lake Risk Active; 5,000+ Rescuers; No Significant Toll Update September 12–14
items.summary: No significant toll update has emerged September 12–14. The confirmed death toll remains at least 1,412: 1,369 in Nepal and 43 in Tibet. The missing-persons count is approximately 5,651 (5,132 Nepal, 519 Tibet). An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat requiring ongoing monitoring. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police personnel continue search and recovery operations. Approximately 75 foreign nationals, including U.S. citizens, remain unaccounted for. Debris has been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. The disaster originated August 27 from a glacier collapse on Langtang Lirung (approximately 5,200 m) that generated a seismic signal of Ms 5.2.

items.source: WMO Global Producing Centres / ECMWF / NCEP / JMA
items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: El Niño at ~3.6°C Niño 3.4 for Sep–Nov; Near-100% Probability of Persistence Through DJF 2026/27; Positive IOD Co-Developing at 0.9°C Amplifying Teleconnections
items.summary: WMO's September 8 Global Seasonal Climate Update for SON 2026 confirms multi-model consensus placing the Niño 3.4 SST anomaly at approximately +3.6°C for September–November — within the range that, combined with atmospheric coupling, defines an unprecedented Super El Niño event. Near-100% probability is assigned to El Niño persisting through both SON 2026 and DJF 2026/27. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) co-developing at a seasonal mean of approximately +0.9°C adds an independent amplifier historically associated with intensified drought in East Africa and Kenya and above-normal rainfall in Australia and parts of South Asia during austral spring and summer.

weather.overview_html: The primary new development on September 14 is in the Eastern Pacific, where Tropical Storm Norbert has weakened to post-tropical status while Tropical Depression 15-E — forecast to be named Odalys — has formed approximately 600 miles south-southwest of the southern tip of Baja California; Odalys is forecast to strengthen and track west-northwestward into the open Pacific, posing no land threat. In South Asia, Pakistan’s PMD peak flooding period September 14–17 is now underway, with heavy rain and urban flooding occurring across Lahore, Gujranwala, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad, and Islamabad; the season death toll stands at 183. The Atlantic basin has reached 105+ days without a hurricane, with the NHC’s Tropical Weather Outlook showing a 20% formation probability for a subtropical area in the central Atlantic — the first any-probability area in weeks, though it is well north of the MDR and unlikely to follow a classic tropical track. The Southeast Asia ASEAN Level 3 haze emergency and Nepal–Tibet rescue operations remain unchanged, and the Mediterranean flash-flood event of September 10–11 remains in post-event damage assessment.

items.headline: Eastern Pacific September 14: Norbert Weakens to Post-Tropical; TD 15-E Forms (Forecast to Become Odalys) ~600 Miles SSW Baja California; El Niño Fueling Continued Eastern Pacific Activity; No Land Threat
items.summary: In the Eastern Pacific on September 14, Tropical Storm Norbert weakened to post-tropical status as it tracked westward into cooler waters and increasing shear. Simultaneously, Tropical Depression 15-E formed approximately 600 miles south-southwest of the southern tip of Baja California Sur; NHC forecasts the system to strengthen and receive the name Odalys as it tracks west-northwestward over open waters. No land areas are threatened. The Eastern Pacific's continued production of named storms — reaching 15 or more — reflects the Super El Niño-driven inverse teleconnection that has simultaneously suppressed the Atlantic to a satellite-era record low and enhanced the Eastern Pacific far above its climatological average.

items.source: Pakistan Meteorological Department / The Express Tribune / NDMA / PDMA Punjab
items.headline: Pakistan PMD Peak Period NOW OCCURRING September 14–17: Urban Flooding Lahore, Gujranwala, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad, Islamabad; Flash Flood Risk KPK, Punjab, AJK; Season Toll 183 Dead / 515 Injured
items.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department-forecast peak flooding period for the 'final monsoon spell' has arrived on September 14. Urban flooding is now occurring across Lahore, Gujranwala, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad, and Islamabad, with heavy-to-very-heavy rainfall falling across major Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa urban centres. The peak risk period continues through September 17. Flash flood risk remains elevated across KPK, Gilgit-Baltistan, Azad Kashmir, and mountainous areas where landslide threat is high. NDMA data as of September 11 reported 183 deaths and 515 injuries since June 26. PDMA Punjab maintains all district authorities on maximum alert. The event reflects the climatological 'final monsoon spell' that typically occurs in mid-September as the South Asian monsoon begins its northward withdrawal.

items.headline: Atlantic September 14: 105+ Days Without a Hurricane — Satellite-Era Record Continues to Extend; NHC Tropical Weather Outlook Shows First Atlantic Formation Area in Weeks (20% Subtropical Low, Central Atlantic, Non-MDR Track)
items.summary: The Atlantic hurricane season's unprecedented drought reaches 105+ days as of September 14, extending the satellite-era record set on September 12. In a minor but notable development, the NHC's Tropical Weather Outlook now shows a 20% formation probability for a subtropical area of low pressure in the central Atlantic. The system is located far north of the Main Development Region — well above 30°N — and is not forecast to follow a standard tropical development pathway; it would be a subtropical rather than a tropical cyclone if it develops. The continuing season suppression is driven by three concurrent factors: the Super El Niño's record upper-level westerly shear across the tropical Atlantic, a persistent Saharan dust plume, and below-normal MDR sea surface temperatures. Five named storms have formed (Arthur through Edouard), none reaching hurricane intensity.

items.source: ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre / Channel NewsAsia / Al Jazeera / Mongabay
items.headline: SE Asia Haze: ASEAN Level 3 Transboundary Haze Alert Remains Active (Since August 26); ~300,000 ha Active Fires Kalimantan; Serian Emergency Continuing; 1.4 Million Malaysian Students Remote; Manila Classes Suspended; Below-Normal Rainfall Through October
items.summary: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre's Level 3 transboundary haze alert, the highest level, first issued August 26, remains in force as of September 14. Approximately 300,000 hectares of active fires in Indonesian Kalimantan continue generating dense smoke, with PM2.5 concentrations above 500 µg/m³ in parts of Sarawak and Brunei. By September 5, haze had reached Sabah and Sarawak in Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, and the Philippines including Manila, where President Marcos ordered class suspensions across Metro Manila and more than a dozen provinces. Serian district's (Sarawak) emergency declaration remains active. Malaysia has kept 1.4 million students in remote learning. Indonesia's BNPB has deployed approximately 12,000 personnel and water-bombing aircraft. Fires have burned approximately 300,000 hectares this season, releasing an estimated 23+ million metric tons of carbon emissions between late August and early September. Below-normal rainfall is forecast for the southern ASEAN region through October.

items.headline: Mediterranean Severe Weather Outbreak POST-EVENT: 2 Dead Italy (Latisana Underpass + Sinalunga Glass); 203 mm/24 h at Lignano Sabbiadoro; Flash Flooding Friuli, Liguria; Evacuations Rijeka (Croatia) and Slovenia; Flash-Flood Season Pattern Now Established
items.summary: The Mediterranean severe weather outbreak of September 10–11 has moved to full post-event damage assessment. Two women died: one at Latisana (Friuli Venezia Giulia), trapped in a flooded underpass despite a Carabinieri rescue; a second at Sinalunga (Tuscany), killed by broken window glass. Rainfall of 203 mm/24h was recorded at Lignano Sabbiadoro and 177 mm at Latisana — extraordinary totals driven by a deep upper-level trough interacting with record-warm Mediterranean SSTs. Flash flooding damaged roads and infrastructure in Liguria and Friuli. Emergency evacuations occurred in Croatia (Rijeka) and Slovenia. The event represents the full realisation of the 'flash-flood season' pattern transition that forecasters had anticipated throughout August as the European heatwave pattern collapsed.

renewables.overview_html: No new major transactions have closed since September 11. The rolling window’s flagship deal remains Skyborn Renewables and Stadtwerke München reaching financial close on September 11 for the 976.5 MW Gennaker offshore wind farm in the German Baltic Sea — a €3 billion-plus non-recourse financing package from 16 commercial lenders and the European Investment Bank (EIB), with long-term PPAs anchored by Amazon (600 MW) and Uniper (100 MW), targeting commercial operations by end-2028. The EIA’s September 9 Short-Term Energy Outlook forecasts record U.S. electricity generation in both 2026 and 2027, driven by solar (generation up 21% year-over-year in H1 2026) and the 3,650 MW SunZia wind farm in New Mexico that commenced commercial operations on June 18, 2026 — the largest wind facility in the Western Hemisphere. The Enel Green Power / Excelsior Energy Capital $760 million solar deal (Faraday 682 MW DC + Skyhawk 128 MW DC) closed September 11, and India continues its record renewable build pace at 16.39 GW added in April–July 2026, on track for ~50 GW annually in FY2026–27.

items.headline: Skyborn Renewables + Stadtwerke München Close €3 Billion+ Financing for 976.5 MW Gennaker Offshore Wind Farm (German Baltic Sea) — Amazon 600 MW PPA; Uniper 100 MW PPA; SWM 25% Equity Stake; Target Commercial Operations End-2028
items.summary: Skyborn Renewables and Stadtwerke München (SWM) reached financial close on September 11, 2026 for the Gennaker offshore wind farm, located approximately 15 km north of the Fischland-Darß-Zingst peninsula in the German Baltic Sea. The financing package totals approximately €2.1 billion in non-recourse project finance from a consortium of 16 commercial lenders and the European Investment Bank, mobilising more than €3 billion of total investment. The project comprises 63 Siemens Gamesa turbines at a total capacity of 976.5 MW. Long-term power purchase agreements include 600 MW to Amazon and 100 MW to Uniper. SWM joined as a strategic equity partner, acquiring a 25% stake in the project. Gennaker is expected to generate approximately 3.8 TWh of electricity annually — enough for around one million German households — with full commercial operations targeted for end-2028. The deal represents the largest offshore wind financial close in the German Baltic Sea to date.

items.headline: Enel Green Power Acquires Faraday (682 MW DC, Utah) + Skyhawk (128 MW DC, Tennessee) Solar Plants From Excelsior Energy Capital for $760 Million — 20-Year PacifiCorp PPA; Meta Energy Off-take; TVA Contract
items.summary: Excelsior Energy Capital completed the $760 million sale of its two largest U.S. solar assets to Enel Green Power North America, closing September 11. The Faraday Solar Plant (682 MW DC / 525 MW AC) in Utah County, Utah carries a 20-year power purchase agreement with PacifiCorp; Meta purchases Faraday's energy attributes to offset corporate emissions. The Skyhawk Solar Plant (approximately 128 MW DC) in Obion County, Tennessee has a long-term PPA with the Tennessee Valley Authority. Combined, the two plants represent approximately 810 MW DC / 625 MW AC of contracted U.S. solar capacity, expanding Enel Green Power's footprint in PJM and TVA service territories.

items.headline: India Clean Power Additions: 16.39 GW Renewable Capacity Added April–July 2026 (14.33 GW Solar + 2.04 GW Wind); BESS Additions Accelerating Faster Than Generation; On Track for ~50 GW Annual FY2026–27
items.summary: India added 16.39 GW of renewable energy capacity in the first four months of fiscal year 2026–27 (April–July 2026), comprising 14.33 GW of solar PV and 2.04 GW of wind. Battery energy storage system (BESS) additions are growing on a percentage basis faster than either solar or wind generation additions, reflecting a policy push to pair storage with intermittent generation. The April–July run rate places India on track for approximately 50 GW of annual renewable additions in FY2026–27, which would be a record and sustain India's position as the third-largest renewable market globally.

items.headline: EIA September 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook: Record U.S. Electricity Generation Forecast 2026–2027; Solar Generation Up 21% YoY in H1 2026; SunZia 3,650 MW Wind Farm Now Operational; Batteries 28% of 2026 Capacity Additions
items.summary: The EIA's September 9, 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook projects record U.S. electricity generation in both 2026 and 2027, forecasting total electricity sales of 4,135 BkWh in 2026 (+2% from 2025) and 4,211 BkWh in 2027 (+2%). Solar generation rose 21% year-over-year in the first half of 2026; wind rose 6%. The SunZia Wind Project — 3,650 MW across 916 turbines in New Mexico, the largest wind facility in the Western Hemisphere — commenced commercial operations June 18, 2026. Battery storage makes up 28% of planned 2026 U.S. capacity additions (behind solar at 51% and wind at 14%). Data center development and manufacturing growth are driving commercial and industrial electricity demand growth faster than residential.

items.headline: Shell Energy Philippines Signs Second 15-Year PSA With Greenlight Renewables for 120 MWp Phase 2 San Isidro Solar (Leyte) — Total Committed Capacity Now 240 MWp Supplying ~100 C&I Customers
items.summary: Shell Energy Philippines signed a second 15-year power supply agreement with Greenlight Renewables for an additional 120 MWp from Phase 2 of the San Isidro Solar Power Project in Leyte, energised July 30, 2026. Combined with Phase 1's agreement, Shell Energy's total committed capacity from the San Isidro project reaches 240 MWp, supplying approximately 100 commercial and industrial customers across the Philippines. The deal is illustrative of Southeast Asia's accelerating corporate PPA market, driven by C&I buyer decarbonisation commitments amid rising retail electricity tariffs.

items.headline: Qualitas Energy Acquires Cero Generation’s Core European Solar Platform From Macquarie Asset Management — 5.8 GW Pipeline Across Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, Finland; Qualitas Becomes One of Southern Europe’s Largest Independent Developers
items.summary: Madrid-based Qualitas Energy completed the acquisition of Cero Generation's core European solar development platform from Macquarie Asset Management, gaining a 5.8 GW pipeline spanning Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, and Finland. Macquarie is retaining Cero's Nordic operations separately. The transaction makes Qualitas Energy one of Southern Europe's largest independent solar developers and reflects continued institutional capital appetite for early-to-mid-stage EU solar development platforms as REPowerEU targets drive pipeline demand across member states.

science.overview_html: The newest entry in the rolling window is arXiv:2609.12815 (September 11): BEAST — a Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer for weather prediction trained at unprecedented scale on the JUPITER supercomputer at Jülich, leveraging 20,480 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs to achieve 3.96 EFLOP/s distributed training throughput; the 700-million-parameter model produces 96-member weight-space ensemble samples for calibrated uncertainty and benchmarks competitive with both ECMWF’s AIFS and operational NWP on extreme weather metrics. The previous window entry is arXiv:2609.11696 (September 10): a head-to-head stress-test of WRF dynamical versus diffusion-model generative downscaling for extreme precipitation at subseasonal lead times up to 3 weeks, finding WRF edges the diffusion model on multicell non-stationary events while diffusion outperforms on stationary supercells — both substantially improving on raw ECMWF. EastAsiaClimateExtremes (arXiv:2609.08241, September 8) provides the first AI-ready weekly S2S benchmark for East Asian extreme heat, rainfall, and marine heatwaves, co-registered with ECMWF S2S hindcasts. The broader period context includes WeatherNext 3 (Google DeepMind, September 3): the first global AI weather model ingesting live geostationary satellite data at 0.1°/hourly resolution, deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, and Earth Engine; arXiv:2609.03210: fine-tuning a graph-transformer with IMERG precipitation data improves medium-range CRPS by up to 19% and outperforms on tropical storm and drizzle events; and CloudCast v2 extending ML cloud-cover nowcasting to 12-hour lead times at 4-km/15-minute resolution, competitive with NWP to 8 hours.

items.source: arXiv / Jülich Supercomputing Centre / JUPITER / Helmholtz AI
items.headline: arXiv 2609.12815 (BEAST): Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer for Weather — 3.96 EFLOP/s on JUPITER (20,480 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs); 700M Parameters; 96-Member Weight-Space Ensemble; Competitive With AIFS and NWP on Extreme Weather
items.summary: BEAST (Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer) is a new global AI weather model from Jülich Supercomputing Centre and collaborators, trained on the JUPITER supercomputer — the first exaflop-class European HPC system — using 20,480 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips across 10,240 nodes. The distributed training achieves 3.96 EFLOP/s throughput via 4D parallelism. The model has 700 million parameters and generates 96 ensemble members using a weight-space sampling approach that produces well-calibrated probabilistic outputs without the computational overhead of explicit multi-model ensembles. On benchmark evaluations for extreme weather events, BEAST achieves skill competitive with ECMWF's AI Integrated Forecasting System (AIFS) and operational NWP ensemble systems. The Bayesian ensemble approach directly addresses a central limitation of deterministic AI weather models: underrepresentation of forecast uncertainty for low-probability high-impact events relevant to the current digest period including Pakistan monsoon flooding and European flash floods.

items.source: arXiv / Bjerknes Centre for Climate Research / University of Bergen
items.headline: arXiv 2609.11696: WRF Dynamical vs Generative Diffusion-Model Downscaling for Subseasonal Extreme Precipitation at 3-Week Lead Times — WRF Wins on Multicell Non-Stationary Events; Diffusion Model More Consistent and Better on Stationary Supercells; Both Beat Raw ECMWF
items.summary: This paper evaluates WRF dynamical downscaling head-to-head against a diffusion-based deep generative model by downscaling ECMWF subseasonal forecasts for two physically distinct extreme precipitation events at lead times up to 3 weeks. Both approaches substantially improve on raw ECMWF outputs. WRF achieves the highest probabilistic skill for a multicell, non-stationary event — the character of the September 10–11 Mediterranean outbreak (203 mm/24 h at Lignano Sabbiadoro, 2 dead) — where the dynamical core's explicit physics captures large-scale forcing. The diffusion model outperforms WRF on a more stationary supercell event and is more consistent across performance metrics overall, suggesting generative downscaling has an advantage where training data provides stronger statistical priors than explicit physics. The study motivates regime-adaptive or ensemble downscaling frameworks rather than a single fixed approach for operational extreme precipitation prediction.

items.source: arXiv / Fudan University / ECMWF / Chinese Academy of Sciences
items.headline: arXiv 2609.08241 (EastAsiaClimateExtremes): First AI-Ready Weekly S2S Benchmark for East Asian Atmospheric and Oceanic Extremes — AHT, Heavy Rainfall, Marine Heatwaves; Co-Registered With ECMWF S2S Hindcasts; Open on GitHub
items.summary: EastAsiaClimateExtremes is an open benchmark dataset providing ERA5/OISST reanalysis-based weekly extreme labels for anomalously high temperature (AHT), heavy rainfall (HR), and marine heatwaves (MHW) over East Asia, co-registered with ECMWF S2S hindcast outputs to enable direct comparison between AI forecasts and dynamical sub-seasonal models. The dataset addresses a critical gap: event-based AI-ready datasets for East Asia at S2S timescales (where dynamical models face the largest skill gaps) have been sparse. Direct relevance to the current period: the SE Asia heat-driven haze emergency and the Pakistan monsoon spell are exactly the type of S2S phenomena this benchmark targets.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03582 (WeatherNext 3): Google DeepMind’s Hourly 0.1° Global AI Weather Model Achieves State-of-the-Art Probabilistic Skill by Ingesting Live Geostationary Satellite Data — Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, Earth Engine
items.meta: Google DeepMind & Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 · September 3, 2026 · In production: Google Search, Gemini, Maps, BigQuery, Earth Engine
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 is the first major global AI weather model to ingest live geostationary satellite data and train directly on raw weather station observations — eliminating the 6-to-7-hour data lag of NWP-based ERA5 initial conditions. It generates new forecasts every hour at 0.1° (~11 km) spatial resolution. On both probabilistic (CRPS) and deterministic skill metrics across the full 10-day medium range, WeatherNext 3 establishes state-of-the-art probabilistic global AI weather forecasting. The model is deployed in production inside Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps, BigQuery, and Earth Engine. The original WeatherNext model became open-source in August 2026.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03210: Fine-Tuning an AI Weather Model on IMERG Precipitation Observations Improves Medium-Range CRPS by Up to 19% — Superior Skill on Tropical Storms and Drizzle Events; First Direct Observational Fine-Tuning for Precipitation in AIWP
items.summary: This paper fine-tunes a graph-transformer AI weather prediction architecture using IMERG satellite precipitation data at 0.25° resolution, instead of relying solely on ERA5 reanalysis precipitation which is itself a model-derived product. The fine-tuned model improves medium-range Continuous Ranked Probability Scores (CRPS) for precipitation by up to 19% over the base model. It also demonstrates superior probabilistic skill for tropical storm precipitation and drizzle events — two regimes where ERA5-trained models are known to underperform. This represents one of the first demonstrations of directly incorporating observational precipitation data into an AI weather prediction model's fine-tuning stage.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03763 (CloudCast v2): AI Cloud-Cover Nowcasting Extended to 12-Hour Lead Times at 4-km / 15-Minute Resolution; Competitive With NWP to 8 Hours; Trained on Copernicus CERRA; Direct Input to Solar Energy Dispatch
items.meta: Nielsen, Bjørk, Dittmer et al. (DTU / DMI) · arXiv:2609.03763 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: CloudCast v2 extends ML cloud-cover nowcasting to 12-hour lead times at 15-minute temporal resolution and 4-km spatial resolution, trained on the Copernicus European Regional Reanalysis (CERRA). It achieves skill competitive with NWP to approximately 8-hour lead times on continuous cloud fraction, and substantially outperforms NWP at 1–4 hours on rapid cloud evolution metrics. Cloud cover is the primary driver of solar irradiance forecast error at sub-day timescales, making 12-hour ML cloud forecasting a direct operational input to solar energy dispatch and intraday grid balancing — highly relevant given U.S. solar additions up 45% YoY in Q2 2026 and Europe's record solar build pace.

items.headline: ECMWF AI Weather Quest Year One Concludes: 42 Teams From 30+ Countries; DJF 2025/26 Hindcast Winner Beats ECMWF’s Own S2S Ensemble; Awards September 24; Year Two to Include Marine Heatwave Track
items.meta: ECMWF Science Blog · September 2026 · Competition: August 2025–September 2026 · Awards: 24 Sep 2026
items.summary: ECMWF's AI Weather Quest — an international AI/ML sub-seasonal forecasting competition — concluded its first year with 42 teams from more than 30 countries having submitted weekly AI-based forecasts for 2-week ensemble temperature and precipitation anomalies globally. The winning DJF 2025/26 hindcast submission outperformed ECMWF's own operational S2S ensemble on the primary skill metric. ECMWF plans to expand the Quest to a second year with longer forecast horizons and a marine heatwave prediction track — directly relevant given the co-developing positive IOD and the SE Asia haze conditions linked to anomalous tropical Pacific SST forcing. Awards ceremony is scheduled for September 24, 2026.

items.title: Premier Energies + RCT India Form 12 GWh BESS Manufacturing Joint Venture in Telangana — India’s Largest Planned Battery Storage Manufacturing Partnership; Rides BESS Policy Push Alongside 16.39 GW FY2026–27 Renewable Additions
items.body_html: Premier Energies, the Hyderabad-based publicly listed solar cell and module manufacturer, and RCT India, a battery energy storage system developer, announced a joint venture on September 11 to manufacture 12 GWh of battery energy storage systems annually at a new facility in Telangana. The partnership positions Premier Energies to extend its supply-chain integration from solar PV manufacturing into the adjacent BESS market, at a moment when India’s BESS capacity additions are growing faster on a percentage basis than either solar or wind generation — reflecting the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy’s push to pair storage mandatorily with large-scale renewable plants under the Integrated Resource Plan. The 12 GWh annual manufacturing target, if fully realised, would represent one of the largest domestically manufactured BESS pipelines in India and would directly serve accelerating state-level procurement tenders for grid-scale storage across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Telangana.

items.title: Pixxel Raises $100 Million Series C (India’s Largest-Ever Space Tech Round) Led by Temasek and Seraphim — Total Raised $195 Million; 6 Firefly Hyperspectral Satellites Operational; NASA and NRO Contracts; Next-Gen Honeybee SWIR Constellation for 2027
items.body_html: Pixxel, the Google-backed Indian space-tech company operating the world’s highest-resolution commercial hyperspectral imaging constellation, closed a $100 million Series C on September 7 co-led by Temasek and Seraphim, with new investors 360 ONE Asset and IMM Investment, and existing investors Radical Ventures and growX Ventures. Pixxel’s six Firefly satellites, all operational in orbit since 2025, capture data across 150+ spectral bands at 5-meter resolution — six times sharper than most existing hyperspectral platforms — enabling methane detection, deforestation monitoring, water quality assessment, and atmospheric composition tracking in near real-time; the company holds contracts with NASA and the NRO. Proceeds will fund the next-generation Honeybee constellation, extending observations into shortwave infrared (SWIR) and adding synthetic aperture radar (SAR) capabilities, with the first Honeybee satellite expected to launch in 2027; total funding now reaches $195 million, making this the largest single space-tech fundraise in Indian history. Pixxel’s hyperspectral data is increasingly positioned as a climate intelligence layer for monitoring ENSO-driven wildfire risk, vegetation stress from drought, and ocean heat anomalies.
items.source_html: Pixxel / SiliconAngle / Business Standard

items.title: Perry Weather Raises $110 Million Growth Investment From Silversmith Capital Partners — Hyperlocal Weather Safety Platform Now Covers 3,000+ Organizations; 50+ Dallas Hires Planned; Total Funding $131 Million
items.body_html: Perry Weather, the Dallas-based hyperlocal weather safety and operations platform, closed a $110 million growth investment on September 9, led by Silversmith Capital Partners with participation from prior investor Arthur Ventures. Total funding reaches $131.35 million. Perry Weather pairs purpose-built on-site hardware weather stations with cloud-connected software to deliver real-time hyperlocal monitoring, automated alerts, and AI-assisted siren activation covering lightning, extreme heat, high wind, and air quality across more than 3,000 organizations including school districts, municipal governments, construction firms, manufacturers, and major professional sports leagues. The company will add 50+ roles through 2027 at its Dallas headquarters and accelerate AI capability development. The round reflects investor appetite for vertical weather-safety software at a time when the frequency of high-impact convective events — relevant to the European flash-flood season and Pakistan monsoon patterns now tracked in this digest — is driving enterprise demand for site-specific alerting.
items.source_html: Yahoo Finance / Dallas Innovates

items.title: WINT Water Intelligence Raises $36 Million Series D to Scale AI-Powered Water Management Globally — LIP Ventures and Inven Capital Co-Lead; 30,000+ Systems Installed; 1.15 Billion Gallons Saved; $100 Million in Water-Damage Losses Prevented in 2025
items.body_html: WINT Water Intelligence closed a $36 million Series D on September 9, co-led by LIP Ventures and Inven Capital (a €500 million European climate tech fund backed by CEZ Group), with participation from existing investors Insight Partners and others. WINT’s AI platform detects and prevents water waste and damage in commercial buildings in real time, reaching more than 30,000 installed systems across nearly 600 enterprise customers; in 2025 it saved 1.15 billion gallons of water and prevented an estimated $100 million in potential water-damage losses across more than 1,300 incidents. Total funding now approximately $105 million. The platform is increasingly positioned as a climate adaptation tool for property and casualty insurers: water damage from extreme-weather-linked precipitation events is a rapidly rising loss category for real estate portfolios exposed to intensifying storms and urban flooding.

items.title: ARC Ride (Kenya) Closes $33.3 Million Series A to Scale Battery-Swapping Electric Motorcycle Network Across Sub-Saharan Africa — IFC, BII, Proparco, Novastar Ventures Lead; 5,000 New E-Motos; Expanding to Ghana, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda
items.body_html: Kenyan electric mobility startup ARC Ride closed a $33.3 million financing round on September 8, comprising a $23 million Series A equity round co-led by Novastar Ventures and Norrsken22, alongside a $10 million debt tranche. Strategic investors include the International Finance Corporation (IFC), British International Investment (BII), Proparco, Musashi Seimitsu, and Talanton. ARC Ride’s Battery-as-a-Service model reduces upfront cost barriers for commercial riders and plans to add 5,000 electric motorcycles and expand from Kenya into Ghana, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda.
items.source_html: TechCabal / Launch Base Africa

items.title: Howden Re Launches International Alternative Solutions Practice — 12-Person Ex-Aon Team; Parametric, ILS, and Climate-Risk Transfer Focus; Sovereign Nat-Cat, Food Security ENSO Triggers, and Transition-Risk Liability Covers
items.body_html: Howden Re formally launched its International Alternative Solutions Practice on September 6, a dedicated unit focused on parametric reinsurance, Insurance-Linked Securities (ILS), and bespoke climate-risk transfer structures, anchored by a 12-person team predominantly hired from Aon’s reinsurance solutions division. Priority markets include sovereign parametric nat-cat covers for Small Island Developing States and lower-middle-income countries, multi-year food security triggers linked to ENSO indices (directly relevant to the record Super El Niño now developing), and transition-risk liability covers for energy companies managing coal asset retirement. The launch reflects tightening traditional reinsurance capacity on climate-exposed lines and rising demand for alternative risk transfer structures from sovereigns and corporates facing event sequences outside historical return periods.
items.source_html: Howden Re / Reinsurance News

items.title: Nexeon (UK) Closes £100 Million Series D for Silicon Anode Battery Materials — National Wealth Fund and Honda Xcelerator Lead; Targets 10,000-Cycle EV Battery Longevity; Teesside Pilot Facility Expansion
items.body_html: Abingdon-based Nexeon closed a £100 million Series D on September 6, led by the UK’s National Wealth Fund (through UKIB) and Honda Xcelerator Ventures, with Korea Development Bank as strategic co-investor. Nexeon’s silicon anode technology replaces or supplements graphite in EV battery anodes, increasing energy density by up to 20% and targeting cycle lives exceeding 10,000 full charge-discharge cycles — critical for next-generation commercial-vehicle BEVs and long-duration residential storage. Funds will expand Nexeon’s Teesside pilot facility and accelerate scale-up toward gigawatt-hour-scale manufacturing. Honda’s participation follows a multi-year joint development agreement signed in 2025.
